Key Points • Tamibarotene plus azacitidine was associated with a high CR rate and a rapid onset of response in RARA-positive newly diagnosed unfit AML. • Tamibarotene-based treatment in AML with RARA overexpression is a novel-targeted approach with potential to improve current therapy. Visual Abstract Abstract A superenhancer at the retinoic acid receptor alpha ( RARA ) gene is associated with RARA mRNA overexpression in ∼30% of non-acute promyelocytic leukemia acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and in ∼50% of myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS). RARA overexpression is an actionable target for treatment with tamibarotene, an oral potent and selective RARα agonist. Sensitivity to the RARα agonist tamibarotene was demonstrated in RARA-high but not RARA-low preclinical AML models. The combination of oral tamibarotene plus azacitidine was evaluated in a phase 2 clinical study in 51 newly diagnosed unfit patients with AML identified as RARA-positive (n = 22) or RARA-negative (n = 29) for RARA mRNA overexpression in peripheral blasts using a blood-based biomarker test. In 18 response-evaluable RARA-positive patients, complete remission (CR)/CR with incomplete hematologic recovery rate was 61%, CR rate was 50%, and time to initial composite CR was rapid at 1.2 months. Transfusion independence was attained by 72% of RARA-positive patients. In contrast, 28 response-evaluable RARA-negative patients had response rates that were consistent with azacitidine monotherapy. Tamibarotene in combination with azacitidine was well tolerated. The majority of nonhematologic adverse events were low grade and hematologic adverse events were comparable to single-agent azacitidine, demonstrating that there was no additional myelosuppression when tamibarotene was combined with azacitidine. These results support further evaluation of tamibarotene-based treatment strategies in patients with AML or MDS with RARA overexpression to provide a targeted approach with the goal of improving patient outcomes. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as # NCT02807558 . Introduction Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) are biologically heterogenous diseases driven by genetic, epigenetic, and functional pathways that may serve as the target for therapeutic interventions. To date, the development of new therapies in AML and MDS has focused primarily on identification and targeting of somatic genetic mutations, cell-surface antigens, and antiapoptotic pathways. 1 More recently, highly active chromatin regions, named superenhancers (SEs) have been described. SEs are large stretches of DNA that regulate the expression of genes through the binding of transcription factors. SE mapping in samples from patients with primary nonacute promyelocytic leukemia (non-APL) AML or MDS, as well as preclinical models led to the identification of a SE associated with the retinoic acid receptor alpha ( RARA ) gene resulting in RARA messenger RNA (mRNA) overexpression. In cells overexpressing RARA , tamibarotene, a selective RARα agonist binds to RARα, saturating unliganded RARα receptors to trigger a transcriptional activation switch to restore myeloid differentiation, inhibit blast proliferation, and promote blast cell clearance in AML and MDS. 2 Tamibarotene (formerly SY-1425) is a next-generation synthetic oral retinoid with improved pharmacological properties over first-generation pan-retinoids, such as ATRA. 3 , 4 In in vitro studies, tamibarotene as a single agent demonstrated antiproliferative effects, induction of retinoic acid response genes, and differentiation effects in non-APL AML cell line models with a RARA SE expressing relatively high levels of RARA mRNA (RARA-high). In in vivo efficacy studies, single-agent tamibarotene demonstrated antitumor activity in RARA-high but not RARA-low AML patient-derived xenograft models. 2 Further preclinical work demonstrated synergy of tamibarotene with azacitidine or decitabine in RARA-high cell lines, whereas there was no additive effect when combining tamibarotene and azacitidine or decitabine in RARA-low cell lines. 5 Concordantly, tamibarotene plus azacitidine produced deeper, more durable responses than either agent alone in a RARA-high AML patient-derived xenograft model. 5 Using RARA mRNA as a biomarker for a RARA SE, a novel blood-based biomarker test was developed to identify patients with RARA mRNA overexpression, classified as RARA-positive, who could benefit from tamibarotene treatment. 6 The clinical investigation of the relationship between the RARA biomarker and the response to tamibarotene was explored in a phase 2 study evaluating tamibarotene in AML and MDS (study SY-1425-201). 7 Early cohorts of the study investigated tamibarotene monotherapy in RARA-positive low-risk MDS, relapsed/refractory (R/R) AML, and R/R higher-risk MDS (HR-MDS). 8 We previously reported that, as a monotherapy, in these cohorts, tamibarotene was associated with clinical activity, as demonstrated by myeloid differentiation ( supplemental Figure 1 ), hematologic improvement, and reduced bone marrow blasts. 8 A marrow complete remission (CR) plus hematologic improvement with both a platelet and neutrophil response was observed in a patient with R/R HR-MDS. 8 The evaluation of tamibarotene monotherapy was followed by evaluation of tamibarotene plus azacitidine in newly diagnosed (ND) unfit patients with AML in this same phase 2 study. 9 , 10 , 11 Herein, we report the mature results from this cohort describing the clinical activity and tolerability of the tamibarotene/azacitidine combination in ND patients with AML with RARA overexpression deemed unfit to receive standard cytotoxic chemotherapy. We describe the development of a novel blood-based clinical assay used prospectively to identify RARA-positive patients who are most likely to respond to treatment, and report correlative analyses of patient samples from this study, identifying the association of RARA-positive AML with a monocytic gene expression phenotype.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigates targeting RARA overexpression with tamibarotene, a selective RARα agonist, in combination with azacitidine in newly diagnosed unfit non-APL acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) patients. It demonstrates that RARA-positive patients respond significantly better to tamibarotene plus azacitidine, achieving high complete remission rates, rapid response onset, and improved survival. The study also explores RARA overexpression's association with monocytic features and its link to venetoclax resistance.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: In a phase 2 clinical study (NCT02807558), azacitidine was administered at 75 mg/m2 (intravenously or subcutaneously) daily on days 1-7, followed by oral tamibarotene at 6 mg/m2 per day (divided doses twice daily) on days 8-28, with each treatment cycle lasting 28 days. This combination was evaluated in 51 newly diagnosed unfit AML patients (22 RARA-positive, 29 RARA-negative). The treatment was generally well tolerated, with myelosuppression rates comparable to azacitidine monotherapy. Hypertriglyceridemia was a frequent, manageable, and reversible high-grade nonhematologic adverse event. No dose-response comparisons were reported for tamibarotene plus azacitidine. For comparative context, azacitidine monotherapy showed similar complete remission rates in RARA-high and RARA-low patients, and venetoclax resistance was evaluated in ex vivo samples without specific dose-response comparisons.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: RARA (Retinoic Acid Receptor Alpha) and its mRNA expression
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Samples from patients with primary non-APL AML and MDS, including peripheral blasts, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (CD34+ and/or CD117+ blasts), primary leukemic stem cell (LSC) samples, primary AML cultures, and pretreatment blood samples (analyzed via RNA-seq and a novel blood-based biomarker test). Public databases like The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Beat AML were also used.
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene Transcript (mRNA overexpression/expression status) and Super-enhancer (SE) association

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, inferior, not associated, enriched, most resistant
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overexpression of RARA mRNA is found in ~30% of non-APL AML and ~50% of MDS patients, often driven by a strong super-enhancer associated with the RARA gene. RARA-positive patients (n=22) showed significantly higher overall response rates (67%), complete remission (CR)/CR with incomplete hematologic recovery (CRi) rates (61%), and a rapid time to initial composite CR (1.2 months) when treated with tamibarotene plus azacitidine, compared to RARA-negative patients (n=29) whose response rates (ORR 43%, CR/CRi 32%) were consistent with azacitidine monotherapy. Median overall survival for RARA-positive patients achieving CR/CRi was 18.0 months (95% CI: 5.7, NE), compared to 5.6 months (95% CI: 0.4, 9.0) for those not achieving CR/CRi. Median OS for all enrolled RARA-positive patients (n=22) was 8.4 months (95% CI: 5.2, 15.6). In some contexts (TCGA), RARA-high patients showed inferior survival (log-rank P = .031) but not in others (Beat AML). RARA expression is highest in monocytic AML (FAB M4: 46%, FAB M5: 67%) and RARA-high status significantly enriches for a high Monocytic Expression Signature (MES) (81% in TCGA, 77% in Beat AML). RARA expression was significantly higher in venetoclax-resistant monocytic LSCs (P = .005) and showed a strong association with venetoclax resistance (ρ = .48). 80% (15/19) of RARA-positive patients were classified as monocytic by MES (>0.5).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: RARA is a nuclear receptor involved in cell differentiation and proliferation, mediating the effects of retinoic acid. Its overexpression, often driven by a super-enhancer, makes it an actionable target for tamibarotene, which binds to RARα to restore myeloid differentiation, inhibit blast proliferation, and promote blast cell clearance. It is also associated with monocytic features in AML.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Used as a diagnostic and predictive biomarker to identify newly diagnosed unfit non-APL AML and MDS patients who are most likely to respond to tamibarotene plus azacitidine treatment. It is also a prognostic indicator for overall survival in AML and is linked to monocytic AML subtypes and venetoclax resistance.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: RARA overexpression indicates an actionable therapeutic target; RARA-positive status strongly predicts higher response rates, more rapid response onset, and improved overall survival with tamibarotene plus azacitidine, serving to differentiate responders. Conversely, RARA-high status is associated with inferior overall survival in some AML contexts (TCGA) and strongly predicts resistance to venetoclax, particularly in monocytic AML, highlighting its role as a key prognostic and predictive biomarker beyond tamibarotene sensitivity. Not associated with a favorable prognosis independently of treatment.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Complete Remission (CR)/CR with incomplete hematologic recovery (CRi)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In 18 response-evaluable RARA-positive patients, CR/CRi rate was 61% (9 CR, 2 CRi), and CR rate was 50%. Time to initial composite CR was rapid at 1.2 months. For RARA-negative patients (n=28), the CR/CRi rate was 32% (7 CR, 2 CRi), consistent with azacitidine monotherapy.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the clearance of leukemia blasts and recovery of normal blood counts, indicating effective disease treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Response to tamibarotene plus azacitidine treatment in newly diagnosed unfit RARA-positive AML patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: High CR/CRi rates indicate therapeutic efficacy and significant improvement in disease status, suggesting a potential for improved patient outcomes in RARA-positive AML.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Signifies improved bone marrow function and erythropoiesis, reducing the need for external blood product support.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Outcome following tamibarotene plus azacitidine treatment in newly diagnosed unfit RARA-positive AML patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Attainment of transfusion independence reflects significant hematologic improvement and enhanced quality of life for patients with RARA-positive AML.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: TCGA RNA-seq data set, Beat AML RNA-seq data set, pretreatment blood samples from ND unfit AML cohort (RNA-seq)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene Expression Signature (surrogate biomarker for FAB status)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: High RARA expression significantly enriches for a high MES (81% of RARA-high patients in TCGA, 77% in Beat AML vs 29% and 37% of RARA-low patients). MES (ρ = .58) is associated with venetoclax resistance in primary AML cultures. 80% (15/19) of RARA-positive patients were classified as monocytic by MES (>0.5) vs 17% (4/24) of RARA-negative patients. Enrichment for high MES (P = 1.2 × 10−5) observed in RARA-positive compared with RARA-negative patients who achieved CR/CRi.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Surrogate biomarker developed to predict the monocytic status (FAB M4/M5) of patient AML blasts.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Prediction of monocytic status in AML blasts (before treatment), association with RARA expression, venetoclax resistance in AML.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts monocytic features in AML, associated with venetoclax resistance, and enriched in RARA-positive AML patients, suggesting a venetoclax-resistance pattern.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene Transcript and Protein Level (Expression level)

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An anti-apoptotic protein, identified as a key gene associated with venetoclax resistance.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates venetoclax resistance; higher expression in RARA-positive patients contributes to a venetoclax-resistance gene expression pattern.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene Transcript and Protein Level (Expression level)

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An anti-apoptotic protein, identified as a key gene associated with venetoclax sensitivity and involved in apoptosis regulation. It is a known venetoclax target.
